Frequently Asked Questions

Tickets & Registration

All tickets include access to both conference days (October 18–19, 2026), all workshop sessions and field tracks, both lunches, coffee and snacks throughout, and the Friday evening reception and gear swap.

Early bird and standard tickets also include the printed Field Notes Live workbook — a field guide–style packet with session notes, speaker bios, reference materials, and blank field pages. Early bird registrants additionally receive priority access to workshop selection when slots open on August 15.

Yes — groups of five or more from the same organization receive 15% off early bird or standard tickets. Email hello@fieldnoteslive.org with your organization name and number of registrations and we'll send you a promo code to use at checkout. Student/community tickets are not eligible for the group discount.

We don't currently offer single-day tickets — the two days are designed to complement each other, and we find the peer connections made on Day One make the Day Two talks much richer. That said, if there's a compelling reason you can only attend one day, reach out before registering and we'll see what we can do. We'd rather have you for half the conference than not at all.

The $95 Student/Community rate is available to:

• Currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate students (student ID may be requested)

• Unpaid volunteers with outdoor education or conservation organizations

• Staff of nonprofits with annual operating budgets under $250,000

• Individual community members who self-identify as community rate eligible

We trust you to self-select the right tier honestly. If you're unsure whether you qualify, email us and we'll help you figure it out.

Yes. A limited number of partial scholarships are available for outdoor educators who would not otherwise be able to attend. Scholarships typically cover 30–60% of the ticket price. To apply, select "partial scholarship" in the registration form or email us directly at hello@fieldnoteslive.org.

Scholarship applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Apply by August 1, 2026 for best consideration. We prioritize applicants from under-resourced programs, rural communities, and programs serving high-need youth populations.

Refunds & Cancellation

Full refund: Cancellations received by September 15, 2026 receive a full refund, minus a $15 processing fee.

50% refund: Cancellations between September 16 and October 1, 2026 receive a 50% refund.

No refund: Cancellations after October 1 are non-refundable, but your registration can be transferred to another person from your organization at no charge.

If Field Notes Live cancels the event for any reason, all registrants receive a full refund within 10 business days.

Yes, registrations can be transferred to another person at any time up to October 14 at no charge. Just email us the name, email, and organization of the new registrant and we'll update the record. The transferred registration must be at the same ticket tier (e.g., early bird cannot be transferred to someone who would otherwise pay standard rate).

At the Conference

Yes, and we mean it. Field sessions on Day One are scheduled outdoors and will run in light rain, cold, and generally imperfect conditions. This is an outdoor education conference — there's something appropriate about the weather being part of the experience.

The only exception is a severe weather alert from the National Weather Service (active lightning, damaging wind event, or similar). In that case, we'll communicate indoor alternatives by 7:30 am on Day One via email and venue signage.

Come dressed for it. See our gear list for packing suggestions.

We do not offer on-site childcare at this time. If childcare access is a barrier to your attendance, please email us — we may be able to help connect you with local options, and feedback like this shapes how we plan future years of the conference.

Day One: dress for outdoor fieldwork. Layers, sturdy shoes or hiking boots, a waterproof layer, a hat, and sunscreen. Temperatures in Asheville in mid-October run in the 40s–50s°F in the morning and climb to the low-to-mid 60s°F by afternoon.

Day Two: the schedule is primarily indoors for talks and roundtables, so you can dress more comfortably. The Closing Circle is outside; you'll want a layer.

See our full gear checklist on the Travel & Venue page.

The Day Two keynote and session talks will be recorded and made available to registered attendees after the conference (typically within two weeks). Day One workshops and field sessions will not be recorded — they're designed as participatory experiences and the learning happens in the room, not on a screen.

The Main Hall, Pavilion, and Conference Rooms are fully accessible. Some outdoor field areas are partially accessible (the River Loop Trail's first 0.8 miles is accessible; the Pine Ridge Area is not). We offer indoor alternatives for any session held in a non-accessible location.

Six accessible parking spaces are located near the main entrance. A hearing loop is available in the Main Hall on Day Two.

For specific accommodation questions, contact access@fieldnoteslive.org before September 15.

Full details on the Travel & Venue page.

Sponsorship

Sponsorship packages start at $750 (Trail Blazer / Bronze) and go up to $5,000 (Canopy / Platinum). Each tier includes exhibition space, tickets, and various promotion opportunities — see the full breakdown on the Tickets page.

To inquire, email sponsors@fieldnoteslive.org with your organization name and the tier you're interested in. We'll get back to you within two business days. Custom packages are available for organizations with specific goals.

Past and target sponsors include: outdoor gear and apparel brands, educational curriculum publishers, conservation nonprofits, environmental consulting firms, state and federal agencies (natural resources, parks services), university programs in environmental education and outdoor recreation, and software tools used in field education, land management, and program administration.

If your organization wants to reach outdoor educators — particularly those working with youth and communities — this is an unusually concentrated and motivated audience.
